title: #004. Minimax Server Utilization
subtitle: Linearize a minimax peak-load objective with an auxiliary epigraph variable.
caseNames: 5 splittable jobs with tighter server restrictions
markdown:
# #004. Minimax Server Utilization

<!-- section:scenario -->
You manage a distributed compute cluster with $S$ heterogeneous servers having compute capacities `capacities[s]` and $J$ splittable continuous jobs with compute demands `loads[j]`. Because of data residency rules, job $j$ can only run fractionally on servers where `allowed[j][s] == 1`.

Each job $j$ must be split completely across its compatible servers ($\sum_{s} x_{j,s} = 1$, $x_{j,s} \ge 0$). Find an assignment minimizing the **peak utilization ratio** across all servers:

$$
\min_x \; \max_{0 \le s < S} \frac{\sum_{j=0}^{J-1} \text{loads}[j] \cdot x_{j,s}}{\text{capacities}[s]}
$$

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P004Input`)**:
  - `loads: number[]` — compute load of each job $j$
  - `capacities: number[]` — compute capacity of each server $s$
  - `allowed: number[][]` — binary compatibility matrix (`1` = permitted, `0` = forbidden)
- **Output (`P004Output`)**:
  - `assignments: number[][]` — `assignments[j][s]` is the fraction of job $j$ routed to server $s$
  - `peakUtilization: number` — minimized maximum server utilization $\max_s u_s$

<!-- section:example -->
With `loads = [12, 8, 10, 6]`, `capacities = [20, 15, 10]` (total demand `36`, total cluster capacity `45`), distributing proportionally gives a theoretical floor of `36 / 45 = 0.80` (`80%`). Even with compatibility constraints, an LP balances all three servers cleanly to **`peakUtilization = 0.8`** (`16/20`, `12/15`, `8/10`).

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Linear solvers do not offer a native `max(u_0, u_1, ...)` operator directly in the objective. Instead, introduce a single scalar auxiliary variable **`z >= 0`** representing the upper bound on every server's utilization (its *epigraph* variable).

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Constrain $z$ to sit above every server's utilization:
`sum_j loads[j] * x[j][s] <= capacities[s] * z` for every server $s$, and simply **`minimize(z)`**! Because we are minimizing $z$, at optimality $z$ tightens down onto the true bottleneck $\max_s u_s$. Don't forget to force `ub: allowed[j][s]` (or `0` when forbidden) and `sum_s x[j][s] == 1`.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{x, z} \quad & z \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{s=0}^{S-1} x_{j,s} = 1 && \forall j \\
& \sum_{j=0}^{J-1} \text{load}_j x_{j,s} \le \text{cap}_s \cdot z && \forall s \\
& 0 \le x_{j,s} \le \text{allowed}_{j,s}, \; z \ge 0
\end{aligned}
$$

The **epigraph transformation** ($\min \max_s f_s(x) \iff \min z \;\text{s.t.}\; f_s(x) \le z\;\forall s$) is one of the most universal modeling idioms in convex optimization.

judge.m0: Output must be an object { assignments, peakUtilization }.
judge.m4: Job {p0} allocation shares sum to {p1}, expected 1.0.
judge.m5: Reported peakUtilization ({p0}) does not match actual max server utilization ({p1}).
judge.m6: Feasible load balance, but peak utilization ({p0}) exceeds minimum ({p1}).
